data.long_meaning: The name Cecily is derived from the Hebrew name 'Kezia', which means 'blind, dark-skinned'. In the Bible, the prophet Isaiah mentions a beautiful woman, the Shulamite, who was once blind but was given her sight by God. The name Cecily may symbolize the spiritual transformation from blindness to enlightenment. The name Cecily carries the meaning “Blind to beauty” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cecily usually hope their child will grow to embody blind to beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Cecily belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Blind to beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cecily total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_greek.name: Κεσίλη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κεσίλη προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα 'Caecilia', που σημαίνει 'τυφλός'. Η λέξη 'caecilia' προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'caecus', που σημαίνει 'τυφλός'. Το όνομα Κεσίλη είναι παραλλαγή του ονόματος Σισιλία, που έχει παρόμοια σημασία. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Κεσίλη έχει πνευματική σημασία και συνδέεται με την αγία Σισιλία, που ήταν μάρτυρας της πίστης.

in_latin.name: Caecilia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Caecilia, from which Cecily derives, comes from the Latin word 'caecus', meaning 'blind'. This name was borne by a 2nd-century Roman martyr, Saint Caecilia, who is revered in the Christian tradition. The name Caecilia and its variants, such as Cecily, have been used in various Christian cultures to signify spiritual blindness to worldly desires and enlightenment through faith.

in_english.name: Cecily
in_english.long_meaning: The name Cecily is derived from the Latin name Caecilia, meaning 'blind' or 'dim-sighted'. This name has its roots in ancient Roman culture and was popularized through Saint Caecilia, a 2nd-century martyr and patron saint of music. In Christian tradition, Cecily symbolizes spiritual blindness to worldly temptations and inner illumination through faith. Historically, the name Cecily has been used in various forms across Europe, reflecting its widespread appeal in Christian societies.

data.cultural_impact: The name Cecily has rich cultural heritage, particularly in the Western world where it was popularized by the Middle Ages. It was the name of several saints in the Catholic Church, including St. Cecilia, the patron saint of music. Her feast day, November 22, is celebrated by musicians and those who love music around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Cecily holds deep spiritual significance as it is believed to represent transformation, enlightenment, and renewal. The name Cecily is derived from the Hebrew name 'Kezia', which symbolizes the transformation from blindness to sight. This spiritual journey can be interpreted in many ways, including the internal journey towards personal growth or the spiritual journey towards a deeper understanding of God. In Christian tradition, St. Cecilia is also associated with chastity, as she never married and dedicated her life to God. This aspect of the name can serve as a reminder to stay true to one's spiritual principles, even in the face of temptation. Ultimately, the name Cecily invites us to cherish the transformative power of spirit and to remember that even in our darkest moments, there is always the possibility of light.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cecily, derived from the Latin name Caecilia, means 'blind' or 'hidden.' In a spiritual context, it symbolizes the inner sight that goes beyond physical vision, or the hidden blessings and talents given by God.

historical_references.reference: Cecily of York, daughter of Richard Plantagenet, Duke of York, and Cecily Neville, was born in 1465 and married Richard, Duke of York, in 1472 at the age of 7. She became Queen Consort of England upon her husband's election as King in 1460. During her brief reign, she was instrumental in the execution of her husband's chief advisor, the Duke of Clarence, on charges of treason.

historical_references.reference: Saint Cecily, a Roman martyr, was a noblewoman who was believed to have been martyred around 177 AD during the persecution of Christians under Emperor Marcus Aurelius. She is the patron saint of musicians, poets, and those who face trials in their lives.
